reasons.A: Short declaratives and fragments with a plain, practical, rule-giving stance and British diction closely match the passage's rhythm without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Clipped rhythm and plain tone fit, but it stacks fragments and aphorisms more thickly than the passage ('Not any more.', 'No hammer.', a list-style plan), so it leans towards caricature.
reasons.B: Long, flowing, subordinate-heavy sentences, reflective hedging and 'faucet'/'container' diction are far from the passage's terse, concrete voice.
